question: The amount on a sum of ₹7,500 at 6% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, in 2 years will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective compound interest rate for 2 years at 6% = 6 + 6 + (6 × 6)/100 = 12.36%

Total amount percentage = 100% + 12.36% = 112.36%

Amount = 112.36% of 7500

Amount = 1.1236 × 7500 = 8427

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8,427.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹7,500

Rate of Interest (R) = 6% per annum

Time (n) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Amount = 7500 × (1 + 6/100)²

⇒ Amount = 7500 × (106/100)²

⇒ Amount = 7500 × (53/50) × (53/50)

⇒ Amount = 7500 × (2809/2500)

⇒ Amount = 3 × 2809

⇒ Amount = 8427

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8,427.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

For 2 years at R%, the effective compound rate is calculated as 2R + (R²/100)%. This allows you to find the total interest directly as a percentage.

Half-Yearly Compounding

If compounded half-yearly, the Rate becomes R/2 and Time becomes 2n periods. The formula adjusts to A = P(1 + R/200)²ⁿ.

Difference Between CI and SI

For exactly 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on a principal P is calculated as Difference = P × (R/100)².
